To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
climate change and its health impacts are perceived by the community in Tanahu.

(1) the majority of respondents had perceived a change to the climate; (2) the majority had perceived a change of temperature and rainfall; and (3) the majority had also perceived a change to disease patterns.

(a) the majority of respondents perceived a change in the climate; (b) the majority of the respondents perceived that there had been an increase in temperature during the summer; (c) the majority of them perceived an increase in rain during the rainy season; and (d) the majority of people perceived an increase in diseases during all three seasons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between perceived climate variability and perceived human health impacts in the Tanahu region of Nepal.
the impact of climate variability on the health of the community in Nepal, a country that is highly vulnerable to climate change.
the perceptions of climate variability among the population of Tanahu district.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the respondents who belonged to the Janajatis ethnic groups and lived in the rural area were more likely to be aware of the climate variability.
climate change has an impact on human health.
community perceptions of climate change and its adverse health impacts are related to socioeconomic status, ethnicity, and type of house.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
climate variability and adverse health effects are perceived by the majority of the population, and there is a need for more awareness and education on climate change and health.
the respondents perceived a change in the climate and that this change was associated with an increase in diseases.
the community is perceiving climate variability and health impacts of the changing climate.

climate change is already affecting the health of people in Nepal.
climate change and variability are perceived to be a serious health threat in the study area and that the community is not confident that the government is doing enough to address these concerns.
